# THE PINNED FUZZ VECTORS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §4.2). A mutant the wire fuzzer
# found once is a mutant it must never have to find again. The random pass is a
# search, and a search that has to rediscover a known red is a search that can
# miss it. Every vector here is seeded into every wire-fuzz run by its own name
# and fed to the leg and the oracle EXACTLY as it is, before the random pass
# starts, so the red it pins is a SEEK.
#
# A vector earns its place by having been a red. It stays as the regression
# gate for the fix that closed it, and its negative control is that fix
# reverted: the run must go red on this vector's name.
#
#   <name> <unit> <root> <file> [message]
#
# The file is a path from the repository root, so a vector may live beside the
# corpus it was mutated from. The trailing `message` marks a vector that is a
# MESSAGE and not a file (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3): its references resolve
# against the unit's announced table, so the FORM is part of what the index has
# to say about it.

# THE COUNT WHOSE OWN SPELLING RUNS PAST THE BODY IT IS FRAMED BY (§3, §4). An
# array body's `L` of 2 is the shortest that carries a header at all, being the
# element kind byte and one count byte, but a canonical LEB128 count is up to
# ten bytes and the header is read against the PARENT buffer rather than
# against the body's own L. A count spelled wide therefore leaves the cursor
# past the end it was framed by, and the span from the cursor to that end is
# NEGATIVE. The reference reads no elements out of it. The oracle sliced with
# it and panicked. Found by the random pass at mutant 99100 of seed
# 24845619678, on Certify run 33887252419.
stream_count_past_body streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/fuzz-vectors/stream_count_past_body.bin

# THE FORGED POINTER CYCLE (§3.1, §14 note 9; schema#535, filed on #521 as
# G-19). One flipped bit in a three-node ListNode chain turns the middle node's
# `next` index from 3 into 2, which is that node's own index. The wire loads,
# the report is all zero, and the loaded node points at itself.
#
# THAT IS THE CONTRACT, NOT A HOLE, and this vector pins it as one. §3.1: "A
# pointer field's payload is a NUMBER: it is bounds-checked and stored, never
# followed... Load itself is safe on any input: it scans, it terminates, it
# fabricates nothing. What a cyclic structure costs is paid by whatever WALKS
# it." The index names a node that exists and whose type matches, so no §4
# event happened and no counter may move. §14 note 9 prices the reader-side
# acyclicity check this version does not spend.
#
# The vector's job here is the REFERENCE AND THE ORACLE AGREEING on that: both
# must accept it with a silent report, and a port that starts following
# references — or one that stops bounds-checking the index — parts from the
# other and this seeks the disagreement rather than searching for it. The
# walking consumers' half of the contract is held beside it, in Go, by
# internal/tablewire's TestForgedPointerCycleLoadsSilentlyAndRefusesEveryWalk:
# the text export and a re-encode each refuse the loaded instance BY NAME, and
# each refusal returns rather than recursing away. Its three negative controls
# are the two guards reverted and a counter added on the load path.
pointer_self_cycle graphdemo Scene    testdata/wire/tables/fuzz-vectors/pointer_self_cycle.bin

# A NODE RECORD OF A TYPE NO POINTER BELOW THIS ROOT NAMES (§3.1, §6.5, §3.3).
# The message form is what makes this reachable: a connection's table announces
# every table's name id whether or not a pointer names it, so a mutated node
# record can claim a type the closure HAS and the root can never point at. In
# graphdemo that type is Layer, which Scene nests by value and nothing points
# at. The reference gives such a record no region storage and skips its body,
# counting one unknown, which is §3.1's rule for a type id this reader cannot
# name. The engine placed it, decoded it, and counted what was inside: four
# unknown against the reference's two, and a region sixteen bytes wider. The fix
# is ir.PointerReachable, in the engine's node table and in the fuzzer's own
# region arithmetic.
#
# THE BYTES ARE THE SECOND ROUND'S. The message form's bodies moved to a packed
# bit stream that a word at a time fills, so the wire the first vector pinned is
# not a wire any more: those bytes decoded to a different shape and the vector
# went quiet. This one is derived against the current stream, a mutant of
# graph_tree_message that the reader with ir.PointerReachable and the reader
# without answer differently: 1 unknown against 3 unknown and 1 kind_mismatch.
# It is the input tables-wire-fuzz-node-type-negative-control replays.
message_node_type_unpointed graphdemo Scene testdata/wire/tables/fuzz-vectors/message_node_type_unpointed.bin message

# A RECORD'S FRAMING IS ITS TYPE ID'S AND ITS PLACEMENT IS THE ROOT'S (§2.5,
# §3.1, §3.3), which are two questions, and this vector is the red that
# separated them. The two RESERVED BLOB IDS say a thirty-two bit length, an
# align and the bytes wherever they appear, because §3.3's tail announces both
# ids whether or not a root names them; ir.PointerReachableBlobs answers only
# whether this root can PLACE such a node. The oracle asked only the second
# question, so with no blob edge under graphdemo's Scene it framed a blob
# record as a TABLE BODY and read its bytes as fields, where the reference read
# the length and refused a record whose 3,739,746,528 bytes run past a 66 byte
# batch. The first vector for this class stopped reproducing when the second
# round moved the bodies to bits; this one is derived against the bit stream,
# found by the random pass at mutant 280820 of seed 24845619678 over
# graph_tree_message. It is the input
# tables-wire-fuzz-blob-node-negative-control replays.
message_blob_node_unpointed graphdemo Scene testdata/wire/tables/fuzz-vectors/message_blob_node_unpointed.bin message

# ILL-FORMED TEXT ON A MESSAGE BODY (§3, §3.3; schema#620). §3's one content
# rule holds over a form-`2` body unchanged in what it rejects, and §3.3 says
# so: a kind `12` payload that is not well-formed UTF-8 is DAMAGE, terminal for
# the batch here because a bit stream has no place to resume. NEITHER ENGINE
# CARRIED IT. The C++ reference's emitted message reader copied the bytes a
# byte at a time with no check, and the oracle's `text` clamped at the raw
# bound, so a body no reader should accept loaded silently into both — agreeing,
# and agreeing wrongly, which is the one shape a differential fuzzer cannot see
# on its own. It became a red the moment one engine was repaired, and this
# vector is what holds the two together from here.
#
# The bytes are `store_full_message` with one byte of `sku`'s payload replaced
# by 0xFF, which is a lead byte UTF-8 never spells. Nothing else moves: the
# length, the align and every field after it are the golden's own, so what the
# two readers answer differently is the content rule and nothing else. Its
# controls are the four in `make tables-message-form-negative-control`, two per
# engine, each of which parts the leg from the oracle on this vector's name.
message_ill_formed_text backenddemo StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/fuzz-vectors/message_ill_formed_text.bin message
